title: GPU node instability — on-call playbook draft
content:
Purpose:
This is an on-call-focused playbook and incident-review draft for GPU node instability incidents we see repeatedly: ECC memory errors, NVLink flaps, nvidia driver crashes, and kernel panics tied to GPU drivers. The goal is: triage fast, mitigate customer-facing impact, capture forensic evidence, and drive durable remediation (FW swap / node retirement / vendor RMA).

Scope and common symptoms observed: 
- Corrected ECC counters climbing rapidly on one GPU (nvidia-smi shows corrected errors)
- Uncorrectable ECC errors causing jobs to fail or GPU to stop answering
- NVLink errors/timeouts in dmesg or nvidia-smi (link reset events, topology changes)
- nvidia driver crash with processes stuck in D state or kernel oops/panic referencing nvidia_uvm or nvidia.ko
- Kernel panic during heavy throughput workloads (long transformer inference batches)
- Intermittent flapping: node becomes unresponsive to k8s probes, kubelet logs show timeouts, pod restarts cascade

Immediate on-call checklist (first 15 minutes):
1) Acknowledge incident and post short incident header in #sre-ops: node name, region, brief symptom. 
2) Isolate traffic: if the node is hosting customer workloads, temporarily cordon and drain (see graceful vs forced below).
   - kubectl cordon <node>
   - kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=10m (if job-critical, prefer eviction with timeout)
3) Attach to node (SSH via bastion) or use remote serial/console if SSH hung. If unreachable, note that and capture last-seen telemetry.

Quick triage commands (copy/paste):
- hostname; uname -a; cat /etc/os-release
- nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,DRIVER,UTILIZATION,POWER,TEMPERATURE
- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,uuid,driver_model.current,driver_model.pending,serial,ecc.mode.current --format=csv
- nvidia-smi topo -m
- sudo dmesg --ctime | tail -n 200 | egrep -i "nvidia|nvlink|ecc|panic|oom|ooops|calltrace|GPU fault"
- journalctl -u kubelet --no-pager -n 200
- sudo cat /var/log/kern.log | tail -n 200 (or /var/log/messages depending on distro)
- for kernel panic: sudo journalctl -k -b -1 | sed -n '1,200p' (collect previous boot logs)

If GPU driver crash suspected:
- Check driver version and loaded modules: lsmod | egrep "nvidia|nvidia_uvm|nvidia_drm"; modinfo nvidia | head
- Try to capture /var/log/nvidia-installer.log and Xorg logs (if present).
- Collect process list and stack traces for CUDA consumers: sudo pstree -p; sudo gdb --batch -ex "thread apply all bt" -p <pid> (only if safe; avoid on prod live if risky)

Mitigation steps (ordered, prefer least disruptive first):
A) Logical mitigation — drain and move workloads off node (preferred).
   - If node responsive: kubectl drain <node> and mark unschedulable until investigation complete.
B) Soft recovery — reload nvidia modules (if node responsive and cluster load permits):
   - sudo systemctl stop kubelet docker/containerd
   - sudo rmmod nvidia_uvm nvidia_drm nvidia_modeset nvidia || true
   - sudo modprobe nvidia uvm
   - sudo systemctl start docker/containerd kubelet
   - Note: this can cause pod-level instability; choose only when node can be taken out of service and restarted later.
C) Reboot node (if soft recovery fails or kernel panic occurred). Collect crash artifacts before reboot (see next section).
D) Hardware fallback — move node to maintenance pool, tag for RMA if ECC/unrecoverable NVLink errors persist.

Evidence capture (very important, collect before reboot if possible):
- nvidia-smi -q (full) redirect to /tmp/nvidia-smi-YYYYMMDD.log
- sudo cp /var/log/kern.log /tmp/kern.log.XXXXX; journalctl -k --no-pager > /tmp/journal-kernel.log
- sudo dmesg --raw > /tmp/dmesg-raw.log
- sudo ls -la /sys/class/drm/; sudo cat /proc/interrupts | egrep -i "nvidia|gpu|nvlink"
- For ECC: sudo nvidia-smi --query-gpu=ecc.errors.corrected.volatile.device_memory,nvidia_smi --query-gpu=ecc.errors.uncorrected.volatile.device_memory --format=csv
- Copy /var/crash or pstore entries (if persistent cpu/pstore configured): sudo ls /sys/fs/pstore; sudo cp -r /sys/fs/pstore /tmp/pstore-archive
- Archive kernel oops messages and coredumps to S3 bucket redwood-sre-gpu-forensics/<node>/<timestamp>

RCA quick template (fill during postmortem):
- Symptom observed: (e.g., Node gpu-rt-23 showed corrected ECC errors on GPU0, then driver crash and kernel oops with backtrace referencing nvidia_uvm)
- Timeline with timestamps (on-call nailed to slack thread and incident doc)
- Root cause hypothesis (hardware ECC aging vs NVLink cable/slot vs driver regression vs thermal/power instability)
- Evidence supporting hypothesis (ECC counters, dmesg, bus error, PCI ID)
- Mitigation performed and immediate customer impact
- Long-term fix and owner (RMA, firmware update, downgrade/upgrade driver, kernel-harden)

Common root causes we've seen and suggested remediation: 
- Increasing corrected ECC counts over weeks => likely memory cell degradation: recommend scheduling node for RMA; mark GPU as failing; avoid swapping in heavy-memory models.
- NVLink errors / link resets visible in dmesg => reseat NVLink interconnects (if on DGX-like chassis) or replace cable / move to different NVLink topology. Track if errors correlate to specific PCIe x16 slot -> suspect motherboard riser.
- Driver regression: recent driver updates (check infra PRs) correlated with multiple nodes showing 'nvidia: GPU fault' and kernel oops. Revert to last known-good driver or apply vendor-recommended hotfix.
- Power/thermal events: high power draw during long batches triggers undervoltage causing GPU hangs; check PDUs and host power rails, and correlate with temp spikes from nvidia-smi.

Observability and alerting improvements (actions to file as followups):
- Alert when corrected ECC errors for a single GPU exceed 100 in 1 hour (SRE-Alert ECC-High).
- Alert when NVLink reset events > 5 in 10 minutes.
- Add histogram of ECC corrected counts per GPU to Grafana; annotate on known maintenance windows.
- Add automated forensic collector runbook (script) that runs when an alert fires to snapshot logs and push to S3 automatically.

On-call notes / tips and gotchas: 
- Don’t rely solely on nvidia-smi during heavy hangs — sometimes nvidia-smi will hang too; capture kernel logs and use journalctl from the host.
- Modprobe rmmod sequence sometimes fails if in-use; a forced reboot may be the safest when multiple GPUs show global faults.
- For kube clusters: graceful drain can time out if pods are unkillable (D-state). Use eviction + force only as last resort.
- If suspecting NVLink, check for firmware mismatch between GPUs and host bios. Vendor docs sometimes require matching firmware sets.

Unresolved questions / open investigations (as of last_modified):
- Are corrected ECC thresholds currently tuned appropriately? Some nodes show steady low-level corrected counts that spike during specific workloads (large seq len). Need product input to define acceptable thresholds.
- Correlation between driver 535.x update rolled out Feb 2026 and spike in kernel oops — infra to track rollout cohorts (PR 398 references this).

Action items (assign owners):
- (Diego) Add automated forensic snapshot script and wire to SRE alerts. Target: 2026-03-20.
- (Maya) Implement Grafana alert for corrected ECC > threshold; create dashboard panel. Target: 2026-03-17.
- (Infra) Compile list of nodes with recurrent NVLink errors and schedule hardware inspection / RMA. Target: 2026-03-31.

Post-incident reporting notes (short template to paste into JIRA):
- Title: gpu-node-instability: gpu-rt-23 — ECC/driver crash — 2026-03-09
- Summary: one-line
- Impact: services affected, error rates, customer calls
- Root cause: hypothesis + evidence
- Recovery steps taken
- Follow-ups: list with owners and due dates

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this doc terse and action-oriented at the top; long forensic dump goes into attached S3 bucket.
- When in doubt, protect customer workloads: cordon & drain early; better to move workloads than to try to hot-fix a flapping node live.

References & search queries: 
- Grafana query examples: avg_over_time(ecc_corrected_total{gpu="gpu0"}[1h]) > 100
- PromQL for nvlink resets: increase(nvlink_reset_events_total[10m]) > 5
- Useful commands: ls -l /sys/class/drm; sudo dmidecode -t baseboard; lspci -vvv | egrep -i "NVIDIA|VGA|PCI"

Change history:
- 2025-11-05 created by Aisha (initial triage checklist)
- 2025-12-12 added ECC thresholds and evidence collection steps (Diego)
- 2026-03-10 updated mitigation ordering and action items after recent incident

If you're on-call now and stuck, ping @oncall-sre in slack with the node name and "gpu-unstable"; someone will co-respond.

End of draft playbook.
